resources.string: Lets apps reach printers and other devices on this network
Lets apps reach local devices. Block connections without VPN can stop this.
Off: all apps use the VPN
Only chosen apps: none chosen, so all apps use the VPN
Android starts Ombra at boot and keeps it on
No app can use the network while the tunnel is down
Only Android can turn these on: tap the gear next to Ombra
Even with both on, Android itself checks the connection and looks for Wi-Fi sign-in pages outside the tunnel.
Ombra can read these after its first connect. Set them under the gear next to Ombra.
Ombra gets the account status from Obscura after the login.
Opens obscura.com in your browser. The link holds your account number, so the browser history keeps it, and a browser with sync can send it to its sync service.
Anyone with this number can use your account. A copy leaves the clipboard after a minute.
Removes the account from Obscura for ever
Obscura deletes the account and Ombra logs out. Time that is left on the account is lost, and Obscura cannot give it back.
Delete the account now? If you log in with the same number later, Obscura makes a new, empty account.
WireGuard inside QUIC. Looks like web traffic and passes most firewalls, but is slower than Speed. Ombra talks to the Obscura API outside the tunnel, so the network can see the API name.
Plain WireGuard over UDP. The fastest, but networks can see and block it and can tell which exit server you use. The relay cannot check that packets come from you.
For networks that block UDP. The slowest: use it only when the other two fail.
A change while connected reconnects at once.
Larger packets are faster. If pages stall, go back to 1280. If they still stall, use Stealth with Small-MTU compatibility.
Gives all packets that this phone sends the same size. Packets from the relay keep their sizes. Uses more upload bandwidth.
For networks that drop large packets. Lowers the speed a little.
Private DNS is set to %1$s in Android settings. Android then sends DNS queries there, so the settings on this page do not apply.
Mullvad DNS blocks these names. This works only on exits that Mullvad runs.
The exit in use is not run by Mullvad, so the block lists do not apply now.
Block lists work only with Obscura DNS: custom servers or network DNS turn them off.
They replace Obscura DNS. Queries go through the tunnel, except to a server on your local network while Local network access is on. The server sees the names you look up.
Enter an IP address, not a name
This address is the phone itself
This address points to no server
A multicast address cannot be a DNS server
This server is in the list already
DNS queries go outside the tunnel. The network sees every name you look up.
This is a DNS leak on purpose: the network you are on, often your provider, sees every name you look up. Use it only where the network needs its own DNS.
All apps except the chosen ones
The chosen apps bypass the VPN
Apps that bypass the VPN show your IP address. Ombra itself always stays outside the tunnel. Changes apply a few seconds after your last change.
Block connections without VPN is on: Android gives apps that bypass the VPN no network at all.
No app is chosen yet. Until you choose one, all apps use the VPN.
Settings, camera and other apps of the phone maker
Ombra uses the new key from the next connect
A new key at the first connect after one day
A new key for each tunnel. A reconnect can take a little longer.
While the exit server sees the same key, it can link your sessions. A tunnel that stays up keeps its key: the new key comes at the next connect, reconnect or disconnect.
The name that the relay connection shows to the network
An extra address for the Obscura API, after the Obscura backup address. It gets your account number and token, also when the Obscura API works, so enter only a host that Obscura publishes.
Enter a host name, for example cdn.example.org
For networks that block Obscura. Leave empty for the default. Both apply at once: a new SNI host reconnects a Stealth or TCP/TLS tunnel.
Compare the exit key with the key of its operator
Saved on this phone for a debug bundle. Applies after a restart. Off deletes them at once.
Collects logs and network tests into one file that you can share
A debug bundle helps to find the cause of connection problems. Read what it does before you make one.

It tests the network from this phone: it contacts apple.com, google.com, the Obscura API and the DNS servers of Cloudflare and Google (1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8) outside the VPN, so they see your real IP address.
It holds the logs of the VPN core, the Android log of Ombra (logcat) and the settings of the VPN core, with network details such as addresses and interfaces.
It leaves out your account number and your private WireGuard key.
The file stays on this phone. Ombra sends it nowhere: you choose where to share it.
For example: no connection on mobile data since this morning
Making the bundle. This can take a few minutes: keep this page open.
The bundle is ready. Ombra keeps only the newest one.
